metadata.title: Effects of anti-aging diets and exercise on age-related musculoskeletal diseases via gut microbiota modulation.
metadata.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This review summarizes evidence on how anti-aging diets and exercise influence age-related musculoskeletal diseases through modulation of the gut microbiota. With population aging, these diseases are public health concerns. The gut microbiota regulates bone, joint, and muscle health via the gut‑joint, gut‑bone, and gut‑muscle axis. Few reviews integrate diet-exercise synergy with mechanistic pathways linking microbial changes to tissue outcomes. DISCUSSION: Anti‑aging dietary strategies, classified into caloric restriction (ketogenic diet, fasting‑mimicking diet, intermittent fasting, time‑restricted feeding) and isocaloric nutrient restriction (e.g. protein or amino acid restriction), reshape gut microbiota composition and function. Caloric restriction and intermittent fasting reduce inflammation and benefit joint and muscle health, whereas long‑term ketogenic or protein/amino acid restriction may adversely affect bone density and muscle anabolism. Moderate exercise increases microbial diversity, enriches beneficial taxa (Akkermansia, Bifidobacterium), and boosts short‑chain fatty acid (SCFA) production, especially butyrate. Exercise also strengthens intestinal barrier integrity, reduces lipopolysaccharide (LPS)‑induced systemic inflammation, and alleviates osteoarthritis (OA), bone loss, and sarcopenia in preclinical models. Combined diet and exercise may provide greater benefits than either alone. However, most evidence derives from animal or small human studies, and causality remains unclear. Future research should clarify causal mechanisms via multi‑omics and germ‑free models. CONCLUSION: This review suggests that both anti-aging diets and moderate exercise may improve age-related musculoskeletal diseases partly through gut microbiota modulation. Given substantial inter‑individual variability, future research should prioritize personalized nutrition and exercise prescriptions tailored to microbiota, genetic background, and lifestyle. These findings inform precision strategies to promote healthy aging.

metadata.title: Culturally Embedded Participation Restrictions in Indian Adults With Knee Osteoarthritis: An ICF-Based Qualitative Study.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify culturally relevant functioning issues experienced by Indian adults with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework. METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study using semi-structured focus group interviews was conducted with 38 ambulatory adults (35-85 years) diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Participants were recruited from physiotherapy outpatient departments and community settings using maximum variation sampling. Interviews were conducted in Gujarati, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated into English and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Meaningful concepts were systematically linked to ICF categories using established linking rules. Dual independent coding and consensus discussions ensured the analytic rigour. RESULTS: This study included 38 participants with KOA. Fifty-five meaningful second-level categories were identified. The most represented components were activities and participation (41.2%) and body functions (29.4%). Frequently mapped first-level categories included mobility (n = 22), neuromusculoskeletal and movement-related functions (n = 9), d6 domestic life (n = 10), community, social and civic life (n = 7) and products and technology (n = 9). Sixteen additional categories not represented in the existing ICF Core Set for OA emerged, particularly relating to culturally embedded activities such as floor sitting, squatting for toileting and religious participation. Environmental barriers, including inaccessible infrastructure and limited rehabilitation services, influenced disability experience. CONCLUSION: Functioning among Indian adults with KOA is influenced by culturally embedded participation demands and contextual barriers that are insufficiently captured in the existing ICF Core Set for osteoarthritis (OA). These findings provide preliminary empirical support for contextual validation of the ICF Core Set for OA and inform potential culturally responsive adaptation for KOA.

metadata.title: Biceps rerouting and derotational radial osteotomy: A technique for correcting forearm supination in NBPBP.
metadata.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Forearm supination deformity is a recognized late sequela of neonatal brachial plexus birth palsy (NBPBP) that can impair functional positioning of the hand and limit activities requiring forearm pronation. Surgical options include forearm osteotomy, tendon rerouting, tendon transfer, and combined procedures. We describe a modified technique combining derotational radial osteotomy with biceps tendon rerouting using cortical button fixation. METHODS: This was a single-patient technical case report. An 18-year-old male with longstanding fixed forearm supination deformity secondary to NBPBP underwent radial derotational osteotomy and biceps tendon rerouting. The biceps tendon was detached with the forearm in maximal supination, rerouted through the interosseous space, and secured with a cortical button with the forearm in maximal pronation. A radial osteotomy was subsequently performed toward pronation with approximately 30° to 45° of rotational correction. Postoperative rehabilitation included protected immobilization followed by progressive range of motion and strengthening. RESULTS: Preoperatively, the forearm rested in approximately 15° of supination, with active pronation limited to neutral and active supination to approximately 50°. Following surgery, the forearm rested in approximately 15° to 20° of pronation. Passive forearm rotation improved from 45° of supination to 40° of pronation preoperatively to 60° of supination to 75° of pronation postoperatively. At 12 months, active pronation improved from neutral to 55° of pronation. No postoperative complications were reported during follow-up. The patient participated in occupational therapy 1 to 2 times weekly during recovery. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates the technical feasibility of combining radial derotational osteotomy with biceps tendon rerouting using cortical button fixation for longstanding supination deformity following NBPBP. The technique provides an additional fixation option for tendon rerouting while addressing the underlying osseous rotational deformity. Given the single-patient design and absence of comparative or biomechanical data, further study is required to determine whether cortical button fixation offers advantages over established tendon fixation methods and to evaluate the reproducibility and clinical efficacy of this approach.

metadata.title: Anatomic feasibility of using Shark Screw tendon for humeral ligament re-construction in medial and posterolateral elbow instability.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Medial and posterolateral rotational instability of the elbow, often resulting from collateral ligament insufficiency, can lead to pain and functional impairment. Surgical re-construction is indicated when conservative treatment fails, yet complications such as graft failure and donor-site morbidity persist. This study investigates the anatomic and biomechanical feasibility of the Shark Screw tendon as a representative human allogeneic bone screw for humeral ligament fixation in cases of elbow instability. METHODS: Eight fresh-frozen cadaveric specimens were used to evaluate the feasibility of the use of a Shark Screw tendon for humeral fixation on both medial and lateral sides. Cyclic loading and failure testing were performed to assess time-zero fixation characteristics and failure load. RESULTS: A total of sixteen testing scenarios were conducted on the specimens. Implantation was technically feasible without anatomic limitations related to implant size or positioning. Six graft failures occurred (38%), all attributable to poor tissue quality. Tendon slippage was observed in 9 of 16 cases (56%) under progressively increasing axial load, while the Shark Screw tendon remained seated. The mean failure load was 101 N (±50) for medial insertions, 118 N (±77) for lateral insertions, and 110 N (±64) overall. After 100 cycles, tendon displacement averaged 1.1 mm (±0.4) during extension-flexion on the medial side, 1.0 mm (±1.0) on the lateral side, and 1.0 mm (±0.7) overall. During supination-pronation, displacement was 0.8 mm (±0.7) medially, 1.0 mm (±0.8) laterally, and 0.9 mm (±0.7) overall. No anchor pullout was observed, although one anchor tip fractured during insertion. CONCLUSION: The Shark Screw tendon appears to be a feasible biologically integrative alternative for humeral fixation in medial and posterolateral elbow ligament re-construction, demonstrating preliminary time-zero fixation characteristics in a cadaveric model. Further biomechanical and clinical studies are needed to confirm long-term outcomes.

metadata.title: Stem cell senescence as a regenerative bottleneck in age-related skeletal degeneration: Mechanistic crosstalk and translational strategies.
metadata.abstract: Skeletal degeneration is a major cause of pain, disability, fragility fracture, and loss of independence in aging populations. Although osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, and intervertebral disc degeneration are usually managed as anatomically separate disorders, they share a common regenerative failure: endogenous stem and progenitor cells lose renewal capacity, acquire inflammatory secretory programs, and become less able to rebuild damaged matrix. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on senescence in bone marrow mesenchymal stem/stromal cells, skeletal stem cells, hematopoietic stem cells, cartilage progenitor cells, synovial mesenchymal stromal cells, and disc-derived progenitor populations. Priority is given to primary mechanistic, omics, translational, and early clinical studies that connect senescence markers with functional impairment or intervention response. We discuss telomere-associated DNA damage, mitochondrial and oxidative stress, nutrient- and mechanosensing pathways, epigenetic remodeling, dysregulated autophagy and mitophagy, and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype as interlocking mechanisms that reshape skeletal niches. Disease-specific sections then examine how senescent progenitor compartments drive osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, and intervertebral disc degeneration through impaired osteogenesis or chondrogenesis, matrix catabolism, inflammatory vesicle signaling, and maladaptive mechanical feedback. Finally, we compare senolytics, senomorphics, metabolic and mitochondrial regulators, cell rejuvenation, extracellular vesicle engineering, biomaterials, and gene-based delivery platforms from a regenerative medicine perspective. Stem/progenitor cell senescence should be treated not simply as a biomarker of aging, but as a compartment-specific therapeutic bottleneck. Translation will require rigorous cell identity, multi-parameter senescence assays, disease-stage stratification, and therapies that restore regenerative competence without suppressing physiological repair.

metadata.abstract: Vatne, EA, Cencer, D, Vatne, M, Pulvermacher, K, Saenz, C, Kraemer, WJ, Robinson, B, Jones, P, Quebedeaux, N, Sprague, R, Dial, M, Carpenter, T, and Hagen, J. Relationship between objective measures of sleep and nocturnal cardiovascular physiology and swimming performance in collegiate female athletes: A Bayesian analysis. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-There is substantial evidence that sleep influences athletic performance; however, relationships with real-world competition outcomes remain unclear. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to explore the associations between objectively measured sleep, nocturnal cardiovascular physiology on the night before competition, and swim performance in female collegiate athletes. Female swimmers (n = 11) who wore a sleep monitoring device the night before competition, competed in the 200-yard freestyle (short course yard), and had ≥21 of 28 prior nights of valid data were included. Sleep metrics included total sleep time (TST), time in bed (TiB), and sleep efficiency (SE), whereas nocturnal cardiovascular metrics included heart rate variability (HRV) and resting heart rate (RHR) standardized as individualized z-scores. Race times were obtained from a publicly available database. Bayesian linear mixed-effects models estimated posterior probabilities of performance improvement. Results indicated a high probability that greater TST and TiB were associated with faster race times, with substantial support for improvements of at least 1 second per additional hour of sleep. In contrast, SE, HRV, and RHR showed low posterior evidence of meaningful associations with performance. These findings extend prior sleep and performance literature that has been confined to proxy assessments of athletic performance in controlled settings to real-world competition that should inform athlete education, emphasizing the importance of sufficient sleep opportunity and duration before competition.

metadata.title: Examining the Impact of Supramaximal Eccentric and Long-Lever Isometric Training Protocols on Isometric Hamstring Strength, Nordic Hamstring Performance, and Sprint Speed.
metadata.abstract: The aim of this study was to compare the effects of a 6-week higher-volume eccentric training protocol with a combined lower-volume eccentric and long-lever isometric protocol on posterior chain strength and sprint performance. Thirty-three NCAA Division II soccer players (men: n = 17, age = 19.7 ± 1.2 years, height = 178.9 ± 6.6 cm, body mass 79.8 ± 8.1 kg; women: n = 16, age = 20.1 ± 0.9 years, height = 166.7 ± 5.2 cm, body mass = 67.0 ± 12.1 kg) were allocated to either group via exhaustive minimization. Nordic hamstring exercise break-point angle (NBPA), rapid isometric hamstring strength (LLB), 20m sprint performance, and continuous angular knee extension velocity waveforms were assessed pre- and post-intervention, and following a 2-week detraining period. A significant main effect of time was observed for sprint, NBPA, and rapid isometric strength (p < 0.05); however, Bonferroni-corrected within-group comparisons reached significance only for sprint performance in both groups, with no significant between-group differences for any outcome. Equivalence testing supported comparable sprint adaptations between protocols but could not be established for eccentric or isometric hamstring strength. All discrete outcome measures were largely maintained or continued to develop following the detraining period though range-specific eccentric strength appeared more sensitive to the training cessation. A combined low-volume eccentric and isometric training approach may represent a viable alternative to higher-volume eccentric programming for hamstring strength and speed development, although this should be approached cautiously to preserve neuromuscular qualities relevant to hamstring injury risk mitigation.

metadata.title: A two-factor framework to assess international male field hockey movement characteristics: Implications for performance preparation.
metadata.abstract: We aimed to establish the nature and structure of the relationships between high-intensity movement characteristics during international field hockey matches. Global positioning system data were obtained from 28 elite male field hockey players (n = 393 international player-matches). Mean and 90% trimmed range were extracted for the 10 most intense 1-min periods (separated by >60s) for: total distance (m); high-speed distance (>5 m·s-1); sprint distance (>7 m·s-1); accelerations (>2.5 m·s-2); decelerations (<-2.5 m·s-2) and high-speed cuts (>45° change-of-direction at >5 m·s-1). Pearson's correlations were calculated for pairs of characteristics (summed across the 10 most intense periods). An exploratory factor analysis was then applied to movement characteristics. Finally, factors were validated by testing whether they discriminated between playing positions using random-effect linear-mixed models. Factor analysis explained 76% of total variance (χ42 = 286, p < 0.001) and resulted in a two-factor solution: 'Distance' (total, high-speed and sprint distance), and 'Acceleration' (accelerations and decelerations). High-speed cuts loaded onto both factors. The two factors also discriminated significantly between playing positions. Our data-driven approach indicates that Distance and Acceleration are distinct factors of international male field hockey, specifically, Midfielders cover more distance than Defenders, and Strikers change speed and direction more than Midfielders or Defenders. Practitioners should consider prescribing and monitoring these distinct factors separately.

metadata.title: The Relationship Between Training Load Metrics and Mental Fatigue in Competitive Male Basketball Players During the In-Season Phase.
metadata.abstract: PURPOSE: This exploratory study quantified the relationship between perceived mental fatigue (MF) and its relationship with training load in semiprofessional, male basketball players during the competitive season. METHODS: Thirteen players (age: 22.1 [3.8] y) were monitored across 15 weeks (longitudinal, observational design). Training load metrics were monitored daily including volume (minutes), session rating of perceived exertion-load, monotony, and strain, quantified over 1-, 2- 3- and 4-week timespans. MF was monitored twice weekly using electronic visual analog scales, and averaged to obtain a weekly MF score. Repeated-measures correlations (rrm) quantified associations between training load metrics and (1) weekly MF and (2) weekly MF z score (zMF). Variables with significant correlations were then inserted in linear-mixed models, to further explore associations. RESULTS: No relationships were evident between training load metrics and weekly MF (all P > .05, trivial). Differently, zMF was associated with weekly volume (rrm = .34, P < .001, moderate), 2-week volume (rrm = .27, P < .001, small), 3-week volume (rrm = .19, P = .019, small), and weekly session rating of perceived exertion-load (rrm = .26, P = .001, small). Linear-mixed model analyses confirmed that only weekly volume meaningfully explained zMF variations (R2 = .11, P = .001). CONCLUSIONS: The small-to-moderate, positive associations between training volumes over 1, 2, and 3 weeks and variations in MF suggest that increased training and game exposure may exacerbate perceptions of MF in semiprofessional, male basketball players. Basketball practitioners may consider manipulating training volumes, especially at the 1-week level, to help regulate the MF among their players.

metadata.title: Public Attitudes Towards Regenerative Orthopedic Therapy.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess awareness, self-rated knowledge, treatment perceptions, and perceived barriers concerning regenerative orthopedic therapies. METHODS: An anonymous, opt-in, cross-sectional online survey of 100 US adults was analyzed using unweighted descriptive statistics. RESULTS: Mean age was 63.5 years; 64% were female. Sixty percent reported prior awareness, while 77% rated their knowledge as little or none. Stem cell therapy was recognized by 84% and platelet-rich plasma by 30%. Physicians were the primary medical information source for 71%; 63% would consider physician-recommended treatment. Seventy-seven percent would pay nothing or less than $500 per session. Perceived barriers included cost (72%), lack of insurance coverage (62%), and doubts about effectiveness (59%). CONCLUSION: Respondents reported low self-rated knowledge, uncertainty about treatment evidence and safety, and financial barriers. Findings support clear, balanced patient communication but are limited by self-selection and the sample's demographic composition.

metadata.title: Jiawei Duhuo Jisheng Mixture Attenuates H2O2-induced Oxidative Injury and Osteogenic Dysfunction in Primary Osteoblasts: An Integrated Target Analysis and Experimental Validation.
metadata.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Oxidative stress-induced osteoblast dysfunction is an important event in osteoporosis (OP). Jiawei Duhuo Jisheng Mixture (JDJM) is clinically used for bone-related disorders, but its molecular basis in OP remains unclear. This study explored OP-related candidate targets of JDJM and evaluated its cytoprotective effects in a hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-induced primary osteoblast injury model. METHODS: Candidate JDJM targets were predicted from its identified constituents and intersected with OP-related genes. The study integrated network-based and enrichment analyses with single-cell mapping, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation. An H2O2-induced primary osteoblast injury model was used for experimental validation. RESULTS: A total of 210 shared targets were identified. Network pharmacology and enrichment analyses implicated JDJM in the regulation of oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, extracellular matrix remodelling, osteogenesis and apoptosis, primarily through the MAPK, JAK-STAT and PI3K-Akt signalling pathways. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis further localized these candidate targets to osteogenic, stromal, vascular, and inflammatory cell populations. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations predicted stable interactions between representative JDJM-derived compounds and selected protein targets. In H2O2-injured primary osteoblasts, JDJM significantly reduced mean DCF fluorescence intensity, increased the alkaline phosphatase (ALP)-positive area and Alizarin Red S absorbance, and partially restored osteocalcin/bone Gla protein (OCN/BGP) protein and Bglap mRNA expression.JDJM was also associated with decreased total JAK1, STAT3, MAPK3, MMP9, and Bad expression and partial restoration of ESR1 expression. DISCUSSION: JDJM attenuated H2O2-induced oxidative injury and osteogenic dysfunction in primary osteoblasts, accompanied by changes in JAK1, STAT3, MAPK3, MMP9, ESR1, and Bad expression. These results support a multi-target cytoprotective effect of JDJM under oxidative-stress conditions, although direct regulation of the corresponding signaling pathways remains to be confirmed. CONCLUSION: JDJM attenuated H2O2-induced oxidative injury and partially restored osteogenic function in primary osteoblasts, accompanied by coordinated expression changes in JAK1, STAT3, MAPK3, MMP9, ESR1, and Bad. These findings support a multi-target protective effect of JDJM against oxidative stress-related osteoblast dysfunction.

metadata.title: Radial pressure wave treatment accelerates recovery from immobilization-induced soleus muscle atrophy and improves ankle range of motion in mice.
metadata.abstract: PURPOSE: Disuse muscle atrophy following immobilization is characterized by decreased muscle mass and reduced joint range of motion (ROM). Radial pressure wave (RPW) treatment is a non-invasive modality that delivers mechanical energy to musculoskeletal tissues, but its efficacy in skeletal muscle recovery from disuse atrophy remains largely unknown. We examined whether RPW treatment accelerates soleus muscle structural recovery and passive ankle dorsiflexion ROM following immobilization-induced atrophy in mice. Furthermore, we investigated the underlying molecular signaling cascades and gene expression profiles associated with RPW-mediated recovery. METHODS: Male C57BL/6 J mice ([Formula: see text] per group) underwent 14 days of unilateral hindlimb immobilization, followed by a 7-day recovery period with or without RPW treatment (1 bar, 10 Hz, 2,000 pulses, three sessions on alternate days). Soleus muscle mass, fiber cross-sectional area (CSA), and passive ankle dorsiflexion ROM were assessed. Candidate genes identified as differentially expressed by exploratory RNA-sequencing in one mouse per group ([Formula: see text]) were subsequently evaluated by quantitative PCR and immunoblotting across all animals in the full cohort ([Formula: see text] per group). RESULTS: RPW treatment increased fiber CSA to [Formula: see text] (vs. [Formula: see text] in the sham group) and improved ankle dorsiflexion ROM to [Formula: see text] (vs. [Formula: see text]). Gene set enrichment analysis revealed suppression of the forkhead box O (FoxO) signaling pathway and enrichment of the extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling pathway. Igf1 expression was higher in the RPW group ([Formula: see text]-fold vs. sham: [Formula: see text]-fold), accompanied by elevated Akt phosphorylation. Col3a1 was uniquely upregulated in the RPW group ([Formula: see text]-fold vs. [Formula: see text]-fold). CONCLUSION: RPW treatment accelerates the recovery of soleus muscle structure and improves passive ankle dorsiflexion ROM following immobilization-induced atrophy in mice.

metadata.title: Relationships Between Isometric Belt Squat Force and Vertical Jump Performance Across Knee Joint Angles.
metadata.abstract: Rebelo, A, Ripley, N, Weakley, J, and Comfort, P. Relationships between isometric belt squat force and vertical jump performance across knee joint angles. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to examine the relationships between vertical jump performance and isometric belt squat force assessed at 2 knee joint angles (120° and 90°) and to compare outcomes across age groups in male and female athletes. One hundred and twenty subjects (20.3 ± 6.5 years, 1.77 ± 0.12 m, 71.0 ± 13.3 kg) performed countermovement jumps, squat jumps, and isometric belt squat tests at 120° and 90° on dual force platforms. Between-group differences were analyzed using 1-way or Welch's analysis of variance with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc analyses. Associations were examined using Pearson's correlations with Bonferroni-adjusted significance thresholds (p < 0.002), while omnibus tests used corrected alpha levels where applicable. Isometric belt squat net peak force demonstrated weak-to-moderate associations with jump height across tasks (r = 0.36-0.55). Associations between net force at 200 milliseconds and jump height were moderate at 90° (r = 0.45-0.52), whereas net force at 100 milliseconds showed negligible associations to jump height. Older athletes produced significantly higher absolute isometric net peak force than younger groups only at 90° knee flexion (up to ∼860 N difference), with moderate-to-large effects (g = 0.67-0.80), whereas relative net peak force did not differ between age categories. These findings indicate that the isometric belt squat can be confidently used to monitor maximal lower-limb force capacity across knee angles, with the 90° position offering greater sensitivity for distinguishing strength levels between age groups.

metadata.title: The Duration of the Repeated-Bout Effect After Eccentric Exercise.
metadata.abstract: The duration of the repeated-bout effect following eccentric knee-extensor exercise remains undefined, despite its widespread use in muscle damage research and training. The present study examined how long this protective effect persists in the knee extensors. Forty-eight young men performed two identical bouts of maximal eccentric knee-extensor exercise (5 × 15 repetitions at 60°/s). Four independent groups performed the second bout 3, 6, 9, or 12 weeks after the first. Isometric torque, range of motion (ROM), delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS), muscle thickness, echo intensity, creatine kinase (CK), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) were assessed before and 2 and 4 days after each bout. Baseline-adjusted linear mixed-effects models were used to compare responses between bouts, complemented by equivalence testing at 12 weeks. The repeated-bout effect was evident at 3 and 6 weeks across most outcomes and remained detectable at 9 weeks for selected markers. At 12 weeks, no significant differences between bouts were observed at either day 2 or day 4 for any outcome. Exploratory equivalence analyses further indicated that the effect was no longer meaningfully present at these time points for isometric torque, ROM, DOMS, muscle thickness, and echo intensity, whereas the findings for CK and hs-CRP remained inconclusive. Overall, the repeated-bout effect may persist for some outcomes for up to 9 weeks, whereas by 12 weeks no meaningful effect was detectable at the assessed post-exercise time points. This time course can guide the design of muscle damage studies and the scheduling of eccentric training sessions.

metadata.title: A rare traumatic triad: Open bicondylar non-conjoint Hoffa fracture with partial tibial tubercle and medial epicondyle avulsions - A case report and biomechanical analysis.
metadata.abstract: UNLABELLED: Coronal shear fractures of the distal femoral condyles are rare intra-articular injuries, and the simultaneous occurrence of a non-conjoint bicondylar Hoffa fracture with a partial anterior tibial tubercle avulsion and a medial epicondyle avulsion constitutes an exceptionally complex traumatic triad. We report the case of a 35-year-old male motorcyclist who sustained this "floating" articular block injury (AO/OTA 33-B3.3) following a high-velocity accident. Diagnostic assessment utilizing Computed Tomography with 3D reconstruction revealed a vertical Letenneur Type II fracture of the medial condyle and a comminuted Letenneur Type I fracture of the lateral condyle, complicated by significant rotational instability. Surgical management prioritized the posterior femoral instability through a double posterior approach, which allowed for direct visualization and anatomical reduction. Fixation was achieved using posterior-to-anterior headless compression screws, augmented by a posterior buttress plate on the lateral column to neutralize shear forces, while the medial epicondyle was anatomically reduced and fixed; the stable partial tibial tubercle avulsion was treated conservatively. At the two-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated excellent functional recovery with 120 degrees of flexion, a Lysholm score of 91, and a successful return to recreational sports. This case highlights the importance of the double posterior approach and "targeted rigidity" in managing multidirectional instability, permitting early mobilization even in the presence of complex extensor mechanism involvement. INTRODUCTION: Coronal shear fractures of the distal femoral condyles (Hoffa fractures) are rare intra-articular injuries, with bicondylar patterns being exceptionally uncommon. A non-conjoint bicondylar Hoffa fracture combined with a partial anterior tibial tubercle (ATT) avulsion and a medial epicondyle avulsion represents a complex, "floating" articular block that challenges standard treatment algorithms. This case report analyzes the biomechanics and management of this rare traumatic triad. CASE PRESENTATION: A 35-year-old male motorcyclist presented with a Gustilo-Anderson Type I open knee injury following a high-velocity crash involving hyper-flexion and valgus stress. CT imaging confirmed a non-conjoint bicondylar Hoffa fracture (AO/OTA 33-B3.3, Bagaria Type 3). The lateral condyle presented as a Letenneur Type I fracture with extensive comminution, while the medial condyle was a Letenneur Type II vertical fracture. Associated injuries included an Ogden Type I partial ATT avulsion and a Watson-Jones Type I medial epicondyle avulsion.Surgical management utilized a double posterior approach to visualize and reduce the posterior fragments. Fixation involved headless cannulated compression screws for both condyles, augmented by a posterior buttress plate on the lateral column to resist shear forces. The medial epicondyle was refixed with a screw and washer, while the stable ATT avulsion was managed conservatively. At the two-year follow-up, the patient achieved excellent functional outcomes, including 120° of flexion, a Lysholm score of 91, and a Tegner Activity Scale score of 7. CONCLUSION: Managing this complex triad requires a thorough understanding of the injury mechanism, which involves coronal shear, valgus stress, and eccentric extensor loading. 3D CT reconstruction is mandatory for planning, and a double posterior approach provides superior visualization for anatomical reduction and posterior-to-anterior fixation. Rigid fixation, particularly using anti-glide plating for the lateral column, permits early mobilization and the conservative management of stable associated injuries, leading to high patient satisfaction.

metadata.title: Extracting meaningful features from time series analysis of plasma analytes in clinical research.
metadata.abstract: While absolute blood biomarkers have long guided diagnosis, their rate of change often provides greater diagnostic value. For the Limb Girdle Muscular Dystrophies studied here, increased muscle weakness is associated with abnormal sarcolemma repair. Time course analyses were made to changes in muscle-derived plasma enzymes after modest physical activity of ambulatory inpatients. Blood samples at 20 selected time points at variable intervals were obtained at rest, and before and after routine morning activities and motor function testing. After these activities, plasma enzyme levels increased in a similar way, suggesting damage and leakage from skeletal muscle. The levels then decreased in a similar way, suggesting that muscle cells stopped leaking and enzymes were subsequently cleared from the blood. The complex temporal changes were modeled using both continuous time and data features to reduce the number of parameters required to describe the irregularly sampled, interrupted, time series data. Unlike individuals with cardiac muscle ischemia or following intense exercise, there was no extended post-injury rising phase of enzyme levels. In contradistinction, levels fell once activity ceased. Time series analyses of blood biomarkers most likely provide an assay and index of sarcolemma fragility and by extension skeletal muscle damage.

metadata.title: Are both hemolysis and impaired myocyte integrity associated with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency?
metadata.abstract: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) is a potent antioxidant enzyme. G6PD deficiency, predominant among males, is a neonatal "neurotoxic" risk, characterized by episodic hemolysis that is sometimes infection triggered. Clinical risk among heterozygous G6PD-deficient females is often under-recognized. Recent reports of rhabdomyolysis among G6PD-deficient individuals are reviewed here. In one case, a male athlete with G6PD deficiency (<10% activity) experienced multiple, acute episodes of rhabdomyolysis, painful muscle symptomatology, injury and hemolysis after strenuous exertion. Both his mother with G6PD-deficiency (<45% activity) and maternal grandmother have chronic histories of episodic or triggered fatigue-related disruptive symptoms. Other case reports of G6PD-deficient individuals with muscle injury and exertional symptoms (with or without hemolysis) showed unique laboratory findings of elevated creatine kinase, myoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, and aminotransferases levels and myoglobinuria. Disrupted myocyte energetics and loss of cellular integrity can be attributed to impaired downstream pentose phosphate pathway (PPP)-related oxidant stress protection, which is a key enzymatic consequence of G6PD-deficiency. These triggered stresses may explain the muscle fatigue and propensity to exertional injury. Correlation between stress-sensitive-impaired muscle injury among all G6PD-deficient individuals, including neonates, requires further clinical validation to ascertain oxidant-stress impact of impaired PPP-dependent cellular energetics of red blood, white blood, neural, and muscle cells.

metadata.title: Beware the Muscle: Silent Exercise-Induced Aminotransferase Elevation as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Hepatology and Pretreatment Screening-A Report of Two Cases.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: In clinical hepatology practice, pretreatment liver enzyme screening plays a key role in making management decisions, such as initiation of antituberculosis therapy or surveillance of chronic hepatitis B. Unrecognized extrahepatic sources of aminotransferase elevations can lead to misdiagnosis, inappropriate treatment alteration, and unnecessary invasive or costly investigations. CASE PRESENTATION: We present two cases of active young males who were undergoing liver biochemical testing for therapeutic decision-making for other underlying illnesses. Patient one was undergoing baseline liver enzyme testing prior to first-line antituberculosis treatment initiation while patient two was undergoing surveillance for e-antigen-negative hepatitis B infection. Both patients had asymptomatic aminotransferase elevations mimicking acute hepatocellular injury. There was a marked and disproportionate elevation of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) relative to alanine aminotransferase (ALT), in the setting of otherwise normal cholestatic and synthetic parameters. Targeted history revealed heavy resistance weight training prior to testing. Measurement of serum creatine kinase (CK) confirmed exercise-induced muscle injury, demonstrating elevated CK concentrations that paralleled the AST trajectory. Cessation of strenuous training led to rapid normalization of aminotransferases and a decline in CK levels, without interruption of tuberculosis management or unwarranted antiviral initiation. CONCLUSION: Clinically silent exertional muscle injury is an underappreciated mimicker of acute liver injury. In patients presenting with isolated or disproportionate AST elevation, confirming a myogenic enzyme source via CK quantification can prevent misdiagnosis, eliminate unnecessary liver-directed workup, and avoid inappropriate modification or initiation of essential pharmacotherapy.

metadata.title: Neuromuscular Fatigue and Recovery: Are Marathon and Trail Running Different?
metadata.abstract: Although trail and road are two running disciplines, they have distinct characteristics potentially leading to different physiological impacts that have never been examined. The aim of the present study was to compare neuromuscular fatigue and recovery between a marathon and two trail runs of equivalent effort (29 km; ± 1,400 m). Forty-one trained runners, specialized in either road or trail running, performed a simulated treadmill marathon (MARASIM), a simulated treadmill trail run (TRAILSIM), or a trail run in natural conditions (TRAILNAT), depending on their speciality. Neuromuscular fatigue, i.e. changes in maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), voluntary activation (VA) and peak twitch (Tw) of the knee extensors (KE) and plantar flexors (PF), blood markers of muscle damage, jump performance, and force-velocity profile (FVP) were assessed before (PRE), immediately after (POST), one (+1 day), two (+2 days), and seven days (+7 days) following the runs. Muscle pain questionnaires were administered at PRE and during the month following the run. MARASIM showed significantly greater decreases in KE VA (-23.5% vs. -9.2% vs. -13.0%) and jump height (-11.7%; +11.4%; +5.9%, for squat jump), and significantly higher increases in blood markers of muscle damage (+1,726 UI.L -1; +641 UI.L -1; +363 UI.L -1; at +1 day) compared to TRAILSIM and TRAILNAT, respectively. The return to baseline occurred later in MARASIM for KE VA and jump height. Muscle soreness values also returned to baseline earlier in TRAILNAT and TRAILSIM compared to MARASIM. No differences between groups existed in KE Pt and MVC, in any PF neuromuscular fatigue variables, and FVP. Overall, marathon running appears to induce greater acute neuromuscular alterations than trail running, mostly on KE, with a slower return to baseline values.

metadata.title: Articular Cartilage-Derived Extracellular Matrix Material Promotes a Pro-Regenerative Macrophage Phenotype to Support Chondrogenesis.
metadata.abstract: Articular cartilage (AC) repair remains a major clinical challenge due to its limited healing capacity and the inability of current treatment strategies to restore long-term function. Biomaterial-based strategies which support favorable immune responses and appropriate progenitor cell function have shown promise in enhancing cartilage regeneration. We and others have previously demonstrated the capacity of extracellular matrix (ECM)-based materials to direct both innate immune cell behavior and progenitor cell differentiation, with these effects highly dependent on the ECM tissue of origin. Building on these observations, we now aim to further investigate the immunomodulatory properties of AC-derived ECM (AC-ECM) materials. Using primary human macrophages, we demonstrate that AC-ECM material promotes a metabolically active mixed response in macrophages, with elevated expression of reparative growth factors conducive to chondrogenesis. Furthermore, AC-ECM limits inflammatory activation of primary human macrophages, as demonstrated by reduced metabolic reprogramming and inflammatory cytokine production. Functionally, macrophages treated with AC-ECM enhance cartilage regeneration by increasing chondrogenic marker expression in mesenchymal stem cells, while also suppressing angiogenic tube formation in endothelial cells. Overall, this work demonstrates that AC-ECM biomaterials can direct macrophage phenotype toward a pro-chondrogenic state, offering a promising strategy for the development of more effective and durable cartilage repair therapies.
metadata.journal: Journal of biomedical materials research. Part A

metadata.title: EMSCs-derived exosomes rescue p75NTR-/- -mediated osteogenesis deficiency via PI3K/Akt/ERK1/2 signaling pathways.
metadata.abstract: The repair of the critical-sized bone defects remains a major challenge for orthopedic surgeons, particularly when osteogenesis is impaired by p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) deficiency. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are not fully understood. This study aimed to clarify the role of p75NTR in bone regeneration and to develop a cell-free approach to rescue p75NTR-/- deficiency-mediated osteogenic deficiency through a controlled releasing of wild-type ectomesenchymal stem cells exosomes (WT-Exo) which were incorporated into silk fibroin/polycaprolactone2:5/polyvinyl alcohol (SF/PCL2:5/PVA) coaxial nanofibrous membranes. p75NTR-/- mice exhibited a reduced bone mass and delayed ossification, while WT-Exo-loaded membranes partially restored osteogenic deficiency in p75NTR-/- cells and enhanced expression of osteogenic markers such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP), collagen type I (Col-I), osteopontin (OPN) and runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2) aaccompanied by activating of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway. Following implantation of the WT-Exo-loaded membranes into the critical-sized cranial defects in p75NTR-/- mice, new bone formation in the defect site was significantly improved by a sustained release of WT-Exo. Overall, the findings in this study highlighted the critical role of p75NTR in osteogenic differentiation of ectomesenchymal stem cells (EMSCs) and demonstrated that WT-Exo, delivered via the coaxial electrospun membranes, represented an effective cell-free intervention method to reverse bone formation deficiency caused by p75NTR deficiency, providing a promising strategy for gene deficiency-related bone diseases.

metadata.title: PTHrP suppresses BMP2-induced osteochondral differentiation and preserves cartilage phenotype in mesenchymal stem cells via inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling.
metadata.abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) has the potential to drive multipotent mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) to undergo chondral-osteogenic (including hypertrophic chondrocyte) differentiation. Parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) plays an essential role in fetal endochondral ossification, although persistent PTHrP stimulation leads to postnatal bone loss. Here, we investigated the effects of PTHrP on BMP2-induced endochondral ossification through hypertrophic chondrocyte differentiation of MSCs. We found that silencing PTHrP expression inhibited BMP2-induced chondrogenic, hypertrophic, and osteogenic differentiation of MSCs, while overexpression of PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs and suppressed BMP2-induced hypertrophic differentiation of MSCs. Using stem cell implantation studies in athymic nude mice, we demonstrated that while MSCs with silenced PTHrP expression exhibited significantly reduced endochondral ossification of subcutaneous cartilage, overexpression of PTHrP promoted the growth of subcutaneous cartilage while significantly delaying ossification, leading to the preservation of cartilage phenotype. Mechanistically, we showed that exogenous PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs by up-regulating Sox9 expression and inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling. Collectively, our findings strongly suggest that PTHrP may play an important role in mediating BMP2-induced chondral-osteogenic differentiation of MSCs by inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling, indicating that PTHrP may be exploited for endochondral cartilage-bone tissue engineering.

metadata.title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification.
metadata.abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1, Zhx3, Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

metadata.title: The associations among athlete status, sleep, and well-being in a large national sample of college students.
metadata.abstract: Objective: College students, specifically student athletes, experience environments that can support and create barriers to flourishing, a form of well-being reflecting positive functioning in relationships, self-esteem, purpose, and optimism. Sleep is one factor that can have implications for student athletes' flourishing. This study explored whether sleep characteristics, including duration, quality, and napping, accounted for part of the association between athlete status and flourishing, as measured using the eight-item Flourishing Scale. Participants: Using the Fall 2022 National College Health Assessment (N = 28,608), structural equation models assessed these associations. Results: Compared with non-athletes, athletes reported better sleep quality, smaller weekday-weekend differences in sleep duration, and longer sleep duration. Athletes also reported more frequent and longer naps. These sleep factors were associated with flourishing although indirect associations were small (β < .06). Conculsion: Overall, athletes reported several favorable sleep characteristics relative to non-athletes, alongside more frequent and longer naps. Sleep remains important in understanding student athletes' flourishing.

metadata.title: The Sleep and Diet of Elite Female Australian Rules Football Athletes Differ With Age and Season Phase.
metadata.abstract: The Australian Football League Women's (AFLW) competition is comprised of a short, intensive competitive season, highlighting the importance of proper fuelling and recovery to support performance. Little is known about the dietary and sleep habits of AFLW athletes across a season, and the influence that age has on these behaviours. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the effects of season phase and age on dietary intake and sleep in elite AFLW athletes. Dietary intake and sleep were assessed in 22 AFLW athletes (25.9 ± 5.0 y) over 10 nights, including five consecutive nights during both pre-season and in-season. Dietary intake was quantified through self-reported food diaries using a smartphone application (Easy Diet Diary), and sleep via a wearable monitoring device (Oura ring). Restricted maximum likelihood mixed models were used to determine variations in dietary intake and sleep in AFLW players between season phases (i.e., pre-season vs. in-season) and age. In-season protein (115.15 ± 35.14 vs. 126.48 ± 40.10 g, p = 0.026) and fat intakes (72.93 ± 29.55 vs. 83.43 ± 33.14 g, p = 0.012) were significantly lower compared to pre-season, with no differences in sleep measures observed between season phases. While age did not influence dietary intake, each additional year of age was associated with 8 min less sleep (p = 0.001) and 4 min earlier wake times (p = 0.032). These findings suggest that protein and fat intakes fluctuate across the seasons, with increasing age being a non-modifiable risk factor for shorter sleep durations within AFLW athletes.

metadata.title: Biomembrane-Camouflaged Stents: Promising Strategies for Advanced Coronary Interventions.
metadata.abstract: Coronary stent implantation remains a cornerstone therapy for coronary artery disease, yet current stent technologies continue to face limitations including acute and late thrombosis, delayed re-endothelialization, chronic inflammation, and in-stent restenosis. These complications largely arise from the nonphysiological interface between the implanted device and the injured vascular microenvironment. Biomembrane-camouflaged stents have recently emerged as a promising strategy to engineer biologically instructive blood-contacting surfaces by integrating natural or artificial membrane systems onto stent platforms. In this review, we summarize recent advances in three major biomembrane-based strategies for coronary stent functionalization: cell membrane-camouflaged stents, liposome-camouflaged stents, and exosome-camouflaged stents. Biomimetic cell membrane coatings retain native bioactive signals that collectively facilitate immune evasion, thromboresistance, and vascular healing. Liposome-based coatings are tunable artificial biomembrane reservoirs for the localized delivery of anticoagulants, anti-inflammatories, nitric oxide releasers, antiproliferatives, and gene therapies. Exosome-functionalized stents further enable bioactive intercellular communication by transferring endogenous regulatory cargos that modulate endothelial regeneration, macrophage polarization, smooth muscle cell phenotype, oxidative stress, and neointimal remodeling. We further discuss fabrication approaches, biological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, translational barriers, and future design principles for these platforms. Although challenges remain in coating durability, sterilization, long-term storage, manufacturing reproducibility, and clinical validation, biomembrane-camouflaged stents represent a compelling direction for next-generation coronary intervention by transforming conventional stents from passive mechanical scaffolds into active regulators of vascular repair.

metadata.title: Bioinspired Mechano-Chemical Titanium Interfaces With Potential for Infection-Resistant Osseointegration.
metadata.abstract: Bacterial colonization and insufficient osseointegration remain major challenges for titanium-based orthopedic and dental implants. Here, we developed a bioinspired mechano-chemical titanium interface by combining an anodization-derived micro-/nano-pitted topography with a polydopamine-citric acid-quercetin (PCQ) functional layer. Inspired by dragonfly-wing micro-/nanostructures, the resulting OPT@PCQ interface exhibited hierarchical topography, enhanced hydrophilicity, and preserved overall mechanical response. OPT@PCQ showed favorable cytocompatibility and significantly promoted osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells, with increased alkaline phosphatase activity, matrix mineralization, and RUNX2, COL1A1, and OCN expression. It also displayed pronounced antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, accompanied by bacterial morphological deformation and reduced viability. Transcriptomic analysis of S. aureus revealed broad perturbation of central carbon metabolism, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, ribosome-associated processes, and stress-response pathways. In vivo, OPT@PCQ promoted wound closure and markedly enhanced new bone formation and trabecular reconstruction in a noninfected rat femoral defect model. Qualitative hemolysis assessment and major-organ histology provided preliminary evidence of hemocompatibility and systemic biosafety under the tested conditions. Collectively, these findings support OPT@PCQ as a multifunctional titanium interface with potential for infection-resistant osseointegration; however, direct validation in an infected bone-defect model remains necessary.

metadata.title: Strontium- and magnesium-doped hydroxyapatite scaffolds enhance bone regeneration by promoting macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype.
metadata.abstract: The development of synthetic bone grafts that integrate osteogenic and immunomodulatory functions represents a critical strategy in regenerative orthopedics. In this study, we fabricated strontium- and magnesium-doped hydroxyapatite (HA/Mg/Sr) scaffolds derived from natural bovine cancellous bone. Physicochemical characterization confirmed the preservation of a three-dimensional interconnected porous architecture (~80% porosity, ~350 μm pore size) with a homogeneous nanoparticulate surface. Doping with Mg and Sr enhanced scaffold degradation, sustained the release of bioactive ions (Ca2+, Mg2+, Sr2+), and significantly increased compressive strength to levels comparable with human cancellous bone. HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds exhibited excellent biocompatibility, promoting adhesion and proliferation of both Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs). While Mg primarily facilitated direct osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs, Sr played a dominant role in directing macrophage polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, as evidenced by increased CD206 and IL-10 expression alongside reduced CCR7 and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α). Notably, macrophage-conditioned medium from HA/Mg/Sr cultures substantially enhanced BMSC osteogenesis, highlighting immunomodulation as a central mechanism. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that the HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds promoted macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype and modulated immune responses through the NF-κB signaling pathway, which was validated by Western blot. In a rat femoral condyle defect model, HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds-particularly those with 10% Sr content (HA/Mg/Sr2)-demonstrated superior bone regeneration, characterized by bone volume fraction (BV/TV), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th), and enhanced new bone ingrowth and integration, accompanied by elevated M2 macrophage infiltration in vivo. Overall, these findings establish that HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds promote bone repair not only via direct osteoconduction but, more importantly, through immunomodulation-fostering a pro-healing M2 macrophage microenvironment in an NF-κB-dependent manner, thereby offering a promising dual-functional biomaterial strategy for critical-sized bone defect reconstruction. This study underscores the therapeutic relevance of targeting macrophage polarization in bone repair and delineates a mechanistic framework for Sr-based immunomodulatory biomaterial design.

metadata.title: Extracellular vesicles: Multi-source regulatory mechanisms in hippocampal homeostasis.
metadata.abstract: Hippocampal health is pivotal for memory, emotional regulation, and cognition. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) facilitate intercellular and inter-organ communication by transporting bioactive cargos; however, traditional research often overlooks systemic influences on the hippocampus in favor of local microenvironmental changes. This review synthesizes evidence demonstrating that hippocampal homeostasis is modulated by the organism's systemic state-including aging, obesity, and immune status-via EVs. We detail mechanisms by which EVs from peripheral organs (adipose tissue, gut/microbiota, lung, bone, muscle, liver, kidney, heart, and spleen) and central nervous system resident cells (neurons, microglia, astrocytes, neural stem cells, and endothelial cells) regulate hippocampal function. These multi-source EVs precisely modulate neurogenesis, inflammatory responses, and synaptic plasticity. Furthermore, we highlight the emerging role of migrasomes as a specialized subset of EVs in this regulatory landscape. By mapping this comprehensive EV-mediated network, we provide a holistic perspective on the crosstalk between the systemic environment and the hippocampus, offering novel insights and therapeutic strategies for diseases associated with hippocampal dysfunction.

metadata.title: 660 nm LED preconditioning programs mitochondrial signaling in BMSCs for functional tracheal cartilage regeneration.
metadata.abstract: Stem-cell-based cartilage regeneration is limited not only by cell delivery, but also by the difficulty of establishing a stable and functionally competent regenerative cell state before implantation. Here, we report a photonic mitochondrial programming strategy in which 660 nm light-emitting diode (LED) irradiation preconditions bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) to enhance functional tracheal cartilage regeneration. BMSCs were seeded onto egg white-derived ring-shaped porous scaffolds and exposed to defined 660 nm LED irradiation before implantation. Among the tested irradiation conditions, 15 J/cm2 optimally promoted BMSC proliferation, chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition, while suppressing fibrotic, hypertrophic and matrix-degrading phenotypes. Mechanistically, 660 nm LED irradiation enhanced cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) activity, mitochondrial membrane potential, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production and respiratory function, accompanied by moderate reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling. This mitochondrial bioenergetic-redox response activated the PI3K/Akt/mTOR/GSK3β-SOX9 axis, thereby promoting type II collagen, aggrecan and glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix formation. Pharmacological inhibition of ROS signaling, mitochondrial activity, PI3K or mTOR attenuated the LED-induced chondrogenic program. In a rabbit tracheal cartilage ring defect model, 15 J/cm2-preconditioned BMSC-scaffold constructs improved cartilage-like tissue formation, airway epithelial repair, lumen patency and mechanical support after 30 days of observation. These findings support 660 nm LED irradiation as a controllable mitochondrial preconditioning strategy for stem-cell-based functional cartilage regeneration.

metadata.title: Clonal articular cartilage progenitors outperform mesenchymal stromal cells in mitigating post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
metadata.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the functional, pathological, and immunomodulatory properties of articular chondroprogenitors (ACPs) with those of bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) in preventing the progression of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) after destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) injury in a mouse model. METHOD: ACP and MSC were isolated from three horses and assessed for their immunomodulatory capacity in vitro. Aliquots of selected ACP clones and MSCs were injected intra-articularly into male mice 1-week post destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM). The functional mobility of the mice before the injury and at weeks 2, 4, and 8 post-injury was assessed by two methods: ANY-maze™ voluntary mobility monitoring and DigiGait™ compulsory gait analysis. Upon euthanasia, joints were collected for histological scoring. RESULTS: In vitro assessments demonstrated that ACPs and MSCs had anti-inflammatory properties: both treatments produced lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, while only the ACPs produced more anti-inflammatory cytokines than controls. In vivo, both ACPs and MSCs lessened the effects of DMM on mobility. Histological scoring revealed significant reductions of PTOA in the medial compartment with ACPs relative to both MSCs and vehicle controls. Overall, ACPs effectively reduced PTOA progression to a greater extent than MSCs. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrated that both equine ACP and MSC treatments provided symptom modification over vehicle controls in a short-term animal study. Notably, ACPs may be more efficacious than MSCs at reducing structural joint pathology.

metadata.title: Flowable and microporous granular grafts made from decellularized extracellular matrix microgels for tissue repair.
metadata.abstract: Decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) scaffolds are widely used in tissue engineering, primarily due to their inherent bioactivity and cell-instructive properties. ECM scaffolds are conventionally prepared as monolithic and rigid sheet-like constructs and while these form factors are generally sutured at the defect site, it can be challenging to achieve even filling of the defect volume, where flowable scaffolds may be beneficial. Although infusible and injectable dECM formulations have been developed, optimizing for high mechanical strength and a porous microstructure that permits integration with host tissue remains difficult. Here, we report the fabrication of granular dECMs, which are flowable and microporous biomaterials that are assembled through the packing of crosslinked dECM microgels. A feature of these dECM microgels is their crosslinking through dityrosine photochemistry, which circumvents the need for chemical modification of the dECM with synthetic functional groups. Granular dECMs show tunable porosity through optimization of microgel packing, and shear-responsive rheological behaviors that impart extrudability from syringe needles. When tested in a mouse model of volumetric muscle loss and compared against no treatment negative controls, bioinert granular controls made with poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate, and bulk dECM implants, granular dECMs showed improved wound healing properties and support robust angiogenesis and myogenesis at a structural level. Data from longitudinal muscle force measurements carried out over 12 weeks showed comparable levels of functional recovery across all groups. Collectively, these results showcase the potential promise of dityrosine crosslinked granular dECMs as acellular injectable grafts for reconstructive surgery and wound healing applications. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Acellular biomaterial grafts made with decellularized tissues are commercially available and clinically used for reconstructive and wound healing applications. Their rigid design and low malleability has motivated the development of injectable and infusible dECM hydrogels. However, it has remained challenging to co-optimize their mechanical properties and microporosity for tissue repair applications. This work presents a granular dECM graft technology that uses light-activated crosslinking of tyrosine groups naturally present in protein-rich tissues to fabricate dECM microgels that are then assembled into microporous scaffolds that flow under strain and can be extruded via syringe into irregularly shaped tissue defects. Using a clinically relevant mouse model of muscle injury, we highlight the regenerative potential of granular dECM grafts in supporting rapid vascularization and myogenesis at the defect site. This advanced design of injectable and flowable dECM biomaterials is likely to find broad utility in reconstructive surgery and tissue engineering applications.

metadata.title: Advances in disease management and treatment outcomes for obesity and knee osteoarthritis in primary care practice.
metadata.abstract: The lifetime risk of developing knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is approximately doubled in people with obesity compared with those without obesity. Many patients with KOA are treated by primary care physicians in the community setting. We performed a targeted literature search on PubMed to identify relevant literature describing the impact of weight loss in patients with obesity and KOA. A strong body of evidence supports the use of weight loss through lifestyle interventions, including caloric restriction in combination with exercise, as a primary intervention in patients with KOA and obesity. Studies show that these interventions are associated with improvements in pain, physical function, and quality of life; however, adherence to lifestyle interventions can be challenging, even with individually tailored programs. Obesity medications, such as glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, are emerging as a new addition to weight management approaches in KOA, with a recent phase 3 clinical study demonstrating the benefits of semaglutide for weight loss in adults with KOA and high body mass index. Although initial data are promising, further clinical evidence is required, and perceived barriers to use need to be addressed before obesity medications can be widely adopted into clinical practice for patients with KOA. Specifically, further data are required to guide decisions regarding optimal treatment duration with obesity medications and to establish their tolerability profile associated with longer-term use. The importance of preserving functional muscle mass in patients with KOA and mitigation of weight regain after obesity medication treatment withdrawal are also identified as areas warranting further research. In this narrative review, we provide practical recommendations to primary care physicians on integrating obesity medications into weight-loss programs, including patient screening, risk stratification, communication, use of guidelines, and the benefits of a multidisciplinary approach.

metadata.title: Molecular drivers of intercellular communication in physical exercise: insights from omics approaches.
metadata.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Physical activity enhances overall health by promoting coordinated communication among organs. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) play a key role in this process by transporting proteins, RNAs, lipids and other molecules that reflect how different tissues respond to physiological stress. Proteomics has been instrumental in clarifying how exercise reshapes EVs, providing insights into their role in mediating intercellular communication and systemic adaptations. AREAS COVERED: Current proteomics of exercise-induced EV remodeling are overviewed and integrated with complementary transcriptomic and lipidomic findings. We highlight modality-dependent changes in EV abundance and cargo, including antioxidant enzymes, metabolic regulators and muscle-associated markers, such as α-sarcoglycan. Methodological challenges in EV isolation, molecular profiling, data normalization, and functional validation are critically examined, along with the potential of EVs as minimally invasive sources of biomarkers and therapeutic vectors. EXPERT OPINION: Circulating EVs transmit information between tissues to support the body's adaptation to exercise. Proteomics has identified important molecular signatures in EVs, but significant gaps remain regarding their cellular origin, the influence of exercise modalities on cargo selection, and the functional roles of these vesicles. Progress will require standardized workflows and integrated multi-omics approaches, combined with functional assays and physiological parameters of exercise adaptation.

metadata.title: Cartilage-targeting engineered probiotic bacterial extracellular vesicles treat osteoarthritis through modulation of matrix homeostasis.
metadata.abstract: Reversing extracellular matrix (ECM) metabolic dysregulation to facilitate cartilage repair represents a key therapeutic strategy for osteoarthritis (OA) treatment. Owing to the avascular nature of joint structures, intra-articular injection is a commonly used clinical administration route. However, the current drug retention time is insufficient to effectively reverse OA progression. In this study, we demonstrated that natural bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are capable of repairing cartilage damage. We modified Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG)-derived BEVs with a chondrocyte-targeting peptide to prolong their therapeutic efficacy. Engineered BEVs, as a drug delivery system, are capable of continuously transporting endogenous miRNAs. Cartilage-targeting LGG-EVs (W-LGG-EVs) penetrate deeply into cartilage tissue and promote extracellular matrix secretion by chondrocytes. Furthermore, W-LGG-EVs were shown to restore cartilage homeostasis and ultimately alleviate stress-related OA. BEVs, as a novel and safe therapeutic agent, hold clinical feasibility.

metadata.title: Evaluation of a four-herb Chinese medicine formula at different concentrations on muscle damage and inflammation in a rat model of DOMS.
metadata.abstract: BACKGROUND: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) impairs exercise recovery, while current treatments remain limited. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulas may provide safe, multi-target interventions. OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the dose-dependent protective effects of a four-herb Chinese medicine formulation (safflower, Chinese Angelica, peach kernel and myrrh) against DOMS in a rat model. METHODS: Thirty-two male SPF SD rats were randomly allocated to control or low- (1696 mg/kg), medium- (3392 mg/kg), or high-dose (6784 mg/kg) groups. The formulation was administered orally for 11 days, with DOMS induced by exhaustive swimming on day 8. Serum CK, Mb, CRP, IL-6, and PGE2 were measured at baseline and at 24, 48, 72, and 96 h post-exercise. RESULTS: The medium- and high-dose groups exhibited significantly lower serum CK, Mb, CRP, IL-6, and PGE2 levels than controls, with the high-dose group showing the largest reductions. The low-dose group showed limited or no significant reductions in most markers, demonstrating a clear dose-dependent protective effect. CONCLUSIONS: The formulation dose-dependently attenuates muscle damage and inflammation in a rat DOMS model, with high-dose treatment achieving the fastest recovery. Clinical trials are warranted to confirm the efficacy and safety in humans.

metadata.title: Role of integrin αvβ5 receptor and microglia in delayed-onset muscle soreness in mice.
metadata.abstract: Delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) is characterized by muscle pain, stiffness, and tenderness following intense or unaccustomed exercise. In humans, symptoms typically arise 6-72 h post-exercise. This study investigated a novel mechanism underlying DOMS, focusing on the involvement of the irisin receptor integrin αvβ5 and spinal microglia in its development. Male C57BL/6 mice were subjected to a DOMS model induced by an acute aerobic exercise protocol, and nociceptive thresholds were assessed using the von Frey filament test. The role of spinal integrin αvβ5 was evaluated via intrathecal administration of the antagonist cilengitide, given both prior to exercise and 24 h post-exercise. To assess irisin's nociceptive effects, it was also administered intrathecally. Additionally, minocycline, a microglial inhibitor, was administered before irisin to determine microglial involvement. An in vitro assay evaluated microglial activation by irisin via flow cytometry. Pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines were quantified by ELISA. Cilengitide reversed exercise-induced DOMS and reduced spinal pro-inflammatory cytokines. Irisin induced nociception, which was attenuated by minocycline. Irisin also activated microglia in vitro, increasing pro-inflammatory cytokine production. These findings suggest integrin αvβ5 and spinal microglia play critical roles in DOMS pathogenesis, with irisin and pro-inflammatory cytokines as key mediators.

metadata.title: Delphinidin induces the upregulation of miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle and miR-23a-3p release from intestinal cells.
metadata.abstract: Delphinidin, one of the major anthocyanidins, inhibits disuse muscle atrophy by increasing the expression of miR-23a-3p in mouse skeletal muscle. However, delphinidin is less stable and poorly absorbed in vivo, so its mechanism of function remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which delphinidin increases miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle. miRNAs can be packaged into extracellular vesicles (EVs) and secreted from cells. We investigated whether delphinidin induces the release of miR-23a-3p encapsulated in EVs from intestinal cells and whether these EVs increase miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle cells. A single dose of delphinidin increased the expression of miR-23a-3p in the small intestine of mice. To examine whether delphinidin affects the secretion of miR-23a-3p in intestinal cells, we used differentiated Caco-2 cells as an in vitro model. Results showed that delphinidin increases the expression of miR-23a-3p in EVs secreted from differentiated Caco-2 cells. In addition, EVs derived from delphinidin-treated Caco-2 cells were taken up by differentiated C2C12 myotubes, resulting in increased intracellular miR-23a-3p expression. Our in vitro results suggest that intestinal cell-derived EVs may contribute to the antimuscle atrophy activity of delphinidin through the delivery of miR-23a-3p to skeletal muscle cells.

metadata.title: Superiority of Tetrapeptide Tyr-Gly-Leu-Phe over Amino Acid Mixture: Mechanisms Underlying Enhanced Systemic Amino Acid Delivery, Anti-Fatigue Efficacy, and Muscle Damage Repair.
metadata.abstract: This study compared the anti-fatigue tetrapeptide YGLF with an equimolar amino acid (AA) mixture across three stages: postingestion absorption, postexercise fatigue, and muscle damage repair. Despite rapid in vitro degradation (<1% intact), YGLF elevated plasma AAs more effectively than the AA mixture 15 min postingestion (51.97 vs 46.34 mg/100 mL). Postexercise, YGLF outperformed the AA mixture by further increasing muscle AAs and blood glucose, reducing metabolic byproducts, and activating AMPK. Following muscle damage, transcriptomics revealed that the AA mixture primarily modulated energy metabolism, whereas YGLF uniquely upregulated muscle growth genes. Western blotting confirmed that YGLF promoted repair via the Sestrin2/mTOR and Pax7/MYOD pathways. These findings demonstrate the distinct bioactivity of YGLF over that of free AAs, establishing a rationale for utilizing specific peptides in sports nutrition and muscle recovery.

metadata.title: Myogenic differentiation-derived small extracellular vesicles as a therapeutic strategy for miR-193b-3p-mediated muscle regeneration.
metadata.abstract: The regeneration of skeletal muscle involves precisely regulated intercellular communication, including extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated processes. In this study, we show that during in vitro myogenic differentiation of human skeletal muscle progenitor cells (myoblasts), miR-193b-3p accumulates within small EVs (sEVs) in a temporally regulated manner. Both sEV-mediated and synthetic delivery of miR-193b-3p enhanced myogenic differentiation in vitro and promoted histological recovery in a murine volumetric muscle loss model. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that miR-193b-3p directly suppresses adapter-related protein complex 2 subunit mu 1 (AP2M1), a clathrin-associated adapter protein that has not been well characterized in muscle biology, and identify it as a negative regulator of myogenic progression. AP2M1 knockdown phenocopied the effects of miR-193b-3p, suggesting that this regulatory axis may contribute to muscle regeneration. In addition, transcriptomic analyses of aged rodent and sarcopenic human datasets revealed conserved upregulation of AP2M1 in degenerative muscle states, supporting its potential clinical relevance. Collectively, these findings reveal a myogenic differentiation-dependent, sEV-mediated miRNA regulatory mechanism that contributes to muscle regeneration. Based on these results, we propose the miR-193b-3p-AP2M1 axis as a potential therapeutic target for muscle-wasting disorders.

metadata.title: DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel reprograms the immuno-oxidative microenvironment to support stem cell-based cartilage repair in osteoarthritis.
metadata.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease, and stem cell therapy is often limited by a hostile joint microenvironment. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and damage-associated cell-free DNA (cfDNA) cooperatively drive innate immune activation, inflammatory macrophage polarization, and chondrogenic instability, forming an immuno-oxidative barrier to cartilage repair. Here, we developed a bioactive DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel (MNKB/HA) to remodel this niche and enhance BMSC-mediated cartilage repair. MNKB/HA integrates Mn3O4 nanozymes with Kartogenin (KGN)-engineered bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) in an injectable hyaluronic acid matrix. Mn3O4 exhibited SOD- and CAT-like activities, scavenging O2·-, H2O2, and ·OH, while efficiently adsorbing cfDNA and CpG-ODN to suppress TLR9/MyD88 signaling and M1 polarization and promote M2 polarization. In vitro, 10 μg/mL Mn3O4 was cytocompatible, protected BMSCs and chondrocytes from H2O2-induced apoptosis, and reshaped inflammatory secretion, with IL-10 increased 8.3-fold and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β reduced. KGN stabilized the chondrogenic phenotype (SOX9, COL Ⅱ, ACAN), while its combination with Mn3O4 synergistically enhanced chondrogenic stability under oxidative/inflammatory stress. In rat OA, intra-articular MNKB/HA reduced OARSI scores, restored COL II and ACAN, decreased MMP13, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and attenuated synovitis and osteophytes. MNKB/HA also reduced synovial cfDNA, weakened TLR9 signaling, promoted M2 polarization, and showed intra-articular retention for at least 10 days without notable systemic toxicity. Thus, MNKB/HA remodels the immuno-oxidative niche through synergistic ROS scavenging and cfDNA adsorption, providing a strategy for stem cell-mediated cartilage repair in OA.

metadata.title: Chaenomeles speciosa-derived extracellular vesicles accelerate fracture healing via orchestrating immuno-angiogenic coupling.
metadata.abstract: PURPOSE: Fracture nonunion remains a major orthopaedic challenge, and dysregulation of the bone immune microenvironment is increasingly recognized as a key pathological driver. Chaenomeles speciosa is a medicinal plant with documented anti-inflammatory properties, making it a promising candidate for immune-modulatory therapy. This study investigated whether extracellular vesicles derived from Chaenomeles speciosa could reshape the immune microenvironment to promote fracture healing. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on human nonunion tissues to characterize cellular heterogeneity. Network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses were used to identify potential therapeutic targets of Chaenomeles speciosa. Extracellular vesicles were isolated by ultracentrifugation and characterized by transmission electron microscopy. Macrophage polarization, angiogenesis, and inflammatory signaling were assessed in vitro using RAW 264.7 macrophages and human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Bone regeneration was evaluated in a rat femoral fracture model using micro-computed tomography and histology. RESULTS: Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed M1 macrophage dominance and enhanced M1-mediated communication with osteoblasts and endothelial cells in nonunion tissues. The IL-17 signaling pathway and matrix metalloproteinase-3 were identified as key therapeutic targets. Isolated extracellular vesicles exhibited excellent biocompatibility, promoted M2 macrophage polarization, attenuated inflammation, and enhanced angiogenesis in vitro. In the rat fracture model, treatment with these extracellular vesicles significantly accelerated bone regeneration, as evidenced by increased bone bridging and callus formation. CONCLUSION: These findings establish a macrophage-centric pathological network in nonunion and demonstrate that Chaenomeles speciosa-derived extracellular vesicles promote bone repair through immuno-angiogenic coupling, supporting their potential as a multi-targeted therapeutic strategy for fracture healing.
